Replacing the Commission's figures with the Receipt Budget's would overwrite one correctly sourced instrument with another and break the internal consistency by which every row of the Commission's own devolution-share table reproduces from its Annexure.

title: "For every rupee we contribute we get back X paise" — the most-quoted number in Indian fiscal federalism is produced by no retrievable instrument, and no body has ever refused to produce it
summary: The sentence organises the politics of Indian federalism, and the quantity behind it does not exist in any published form. Its denominator — what a state contributes to the Union exchequer — has three components in three different states. State-wise direct tax is published annually by the Central Board of Direct Taxes. State-wise goods and services tax is published monthly. State-wise indirect tax other than the goods and services tax is stated by the Government, five times in sixteen years across both Houses and by three different Ministers, to be "not maintained". Nobody adds the three. Nobody has ever been refused them. Everyone who has asked has been given something else instead.
whatHappened: THE STATED REASON, AND WHY THIS RECORD TAKES IT AS not-collected. The schema records the reason the responsible body gives, not the reason that is true. The responsible body has given one, consistently: "State-wise data on collection of Indirect Taxes (Customs/Central Excise/Service Tax) is not maintained" (Rajya Sabha, 13 December 2022); "not maintained Centrally" (Rajya Sabha, 5 December 2023); "However, in case of Indirect Taxes State-wise data is not maintained" (Lok Sabha, 24 March 2025, and Rajya Sabha, 10 March 2026, word for word identical); and, fifteen years earlier and before the goods and services tax existed, "The State-wise details of the said amount are not being maintained" (16 November 2010). Not maintained is a not-collected statement in the holder's own words: nothing was gathered, so there is nothing to release. WHY NOT never-defined. Two arguments were put for it in this run and neither carries. The first rests on a single sentence in a single parliamentary answer of 3 February 2020, that there is no mechanism for transfer of revenue by states to the Centre with regard to central taxes — AN ANSWER THIS DROP DOES NOT HOLD, whose URL was not carried into any retrieved part, so nothing here rests on it and it is recorded only as an argument raised and rejected. It would not carry even if held: the sentence denies a transfer MECHANISM and not a DEFINITION, the Centre collects these taxes directly so no transfer exists to describe, and the answer is reported to annex the state-wise devolution table beneath it. The second is stronger and is built on documents that were retrieved — the Union's own goods and services tax FAQ, which says place of supply is fixed by "proxies or assumptions" chosen for whichever "gives more appropriate result than others", and that "the same element may flow to more than one location". That is a real difficulty about INTERPRETING an attribution, and the Union then settles it by statute; a stipulated rule is still an agreed definition. never-defined requires that the quantity could not be collected even in principle, and it plainly could: the first seven Finance Commissions used contribution to tax revenues as a devolution criterion with numeric weights of 10 or 20 per cent, and the Ninth used it last — roughly forty years of constitutional practice in which the quantity was defined, measured and used to move money. The Union also defends the integrity of its own state-wise direct-tax attribution when challenged, ranked states by indirect-tax collection when asked about tobacco in 2023, and in 2005 undertook to lay the whole quantity for Gujarat on the Table of the House. WHY NOT withheld. That value requires an identifiable refusal. Across more than ten dated, specific requests in both Houses there is not one. What the record shows instead is SUBSTITUTION: asked whether Tamil Nadu receives less than 29 paise per rupee and for "the details of tax devolution per one Rupee received, State-wise", the Government returned the inter-se percentage share of the divisible pool (4.079 per cent) and neither confirmed nor denied the figure; asked for "exact percentage devolved to states from total central revenue", it recited Articles 270 and 271; asked about Tamil Nadu's declining share "despite the State being among the highest contributors", it answered with share and per-capita transfers and said the question "does not arise"; asked for central taxes and cess collected from Karnataka, it supplied gross goods and services tax and devolution and never mentioned the rest, not even to say it was not maintained. Four substitutions, zero refusals. Substitution has no slot in the four-value enum and this record does not propose one; it is stated here as an observation about the shape of the record. WHY THE DISPUTE FLAG. The blanket sentence is false of part of its own scope: the goods and services tax is an indirect tax, and the Ministry of Finance publishes state-wise goods and services tax collection every month. Two of the five answers in fact supply it in an annexure while the sentence beside it says state-wise indirect-tax data is not maintained. The claim is true of customs, union excise and service tax and false of the goods and services tax as stated. THE STATES DO NOT ASK FOR IT EITHER. Annexure 8.1 of the Sixteenth Finance Commission's second volume tabulates the devolution criteria proposed by all twenty-eight states across nineteen columns. Not one is based on Union tax contributed — not from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka or Maharashtra, whose public politics most rests on the claim. Where states use the word contribution the referent is output: agricultural gross value added, mining gross value added, incremental gross state domestic product. The Commission itself, asked in 2026 to reward contribution, reached for share of gross domestic product at a weight of 10 per cent rather than for tax paid, and the word derivation appears zero times in its main report against a positive control of fifty-seven for collection.
assessmentNote: No objective was ever stated by anyone to produce this quantity, so there is nothing to score. The value asserts nothing about the finding's firmness: the absence is established across both Houses from 1995 to 2026 with positive controls on every negative, and the two published components were retrieved and read.
caseFor: The Constitution does not distribute Union revenue by contribution and never has since the Seventh Finance Commission, so the quantity is not one the Union is obliged to produce or a Commission obliged to use. Union taxes are levied by the Union under Articles 268 to 271 and are not transferred by states to the Centre; there is no remittance from a state to be counted. Under the goods and services tax the objection is definitional rather than administrative: the tax is destination-based by statute, the settlement machinery exists precisely to move revenue away from where it was collected, and the Union publishes both the pre-settlement and post-settlement columns side by side so the difference is visible. The Union does publish what it can — state-wise direct tax annually for seven years, state-wise goods and services tax monthly — and the component it says it does not keep is genuinely the residue: customs collected at ports serving many states, and union excise collected at factory gates. And the states themselves, given a formal opportunity to propose any criterion they wished, proposed nineteen and did not propose this one.
caseAgainst: A figure that no instrument produces governs the argument anyway, and the body that could settle it has been asked more than ten times over twenty-five years by members of at least eight parties about at least eight states and has answered in the form asked not once. The stated reason will not bear its own weight: it is given as a blanket claim about indirect taxes while the same Ministry publishes state-wise goods and services tax every month, and two of the five answers supply it in an annexure to the very reply that denies keeping it. What is published is published without warning: the Central Board of Direct Taxes prints a state-wise rupee table whose attribution key — disclosed only in a footnote explaining the residual buckets — is the state code in the assessee's communication address, which is why Maharashtra alone is 40.3 per cent of the national total, and a full-text search of the document for disclaim, caution, should not, not be construed, head office or registered office returns nothing. Roughly 30.7 per cent of gross goods and services tax has no state line at all. And the one occasion on which the Government accepted that the quantity could be produced — the 2005 undertaking to collect the information for Gujarat and lay it before the House — has no traceable outcome.
differentFactsNote: The two sides count different things and neither contradicts the other's facts. The Union's case is constitutional and procedural: Article 270 and Article 271 confer the levy, no transfer from state to Centre exists, and no Commission since the Ninth has used a contribution criterion — all of which is true and none of which is a quantity. The states' case is about a magnitude: that what they put in exceeds what they get back. Granting the Union's constitutional facts in full leaves the states' claim entirely intact, and granting the states' magnitude in full leaves the Union's constitutional position untouched. No common ledger can be built, and the reason is not that nobody has built it: one of the three inputs the ledger needs is declared by its holder not to exist, so the comparison is not merely unbuilt but blocked at the source. That is the condition this field exists for.

unmeasured.what: The ratio of Union transfers received to Union taxes contributed, for any state, in any year — the quantity the phrase "X paise in the rupee" names
unmeasured.why: No instrument computes it. The stated reason is the Government's own, given five times in sixteen years and in both Houses: state-wise data on collection of indirect taxes is not maintained, so one of the ratio's inputs does not exist to be divided into anything. The reason is DISPUTED for part of its scope, and the contradiction is the schema's own illustrative case: the goods and services tax is an indirect tax and the Ministry of Finance publishes state-wise goods and services tax collection every month, including in annexures to two of the five answers that deny keeping it. The claim holds for customs, union excise and service tax and fails for the goods and services tax as worded. NOT never-defined: the quantity was defined, measured and given numeric weight by nine Finance Commissions from 1952 to about 1990, and no body has ever told Parliament it cannot be defined. NOT withheld: more than ten dated, specific requests in both Houses produced four substitutions, one recital of the constitutional articles, one silent omission and one undertaking to supply — and zero refusals. What the record actually shows is substitution, for which the four-value enum has no slot; that is recorded here as an observation and no enum value is proposed.
unmeasured.wouldFill: Any one of four things, in descending order of value. A laid paper fulfilling the undertaking of 1 March 2005 to collect and lay revenue collected from Gujarat directly and indirectly — laid papers were outside the reach of the question-search endpoints used here, so this is an open thread and not a closed negative. Any of five directly on-point answers that are unretrievable today because of a systemic archive defect rather than any act of suppression: Rajya Sabha Q.2833 (Maharashtra, 5 August 2014), Q.211 and Q.192 (Tamil Nadu, 22 and 8 July 2014), Starred Q.8 (Punjab, 22 November 2011) and Lok Sabha Q.1801 (24 August 2007) — the retrieval path was proved first, on downloadable sibling files in the same directory, and the session carries filenames for only 31 per cent of its records against 99.9 per cent for a comparison session. A published state-wise series for customs, union excise and service tax on a stated basis, which the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs could produce as the Central Board of Direct Taxes already does. Or an explicit official statement that the quantity cannot be attributed at all, which would move the value to never-defined immediately.

unmeasured.what: A state's total contribution to the Union exchequer across all tax heads — the denominator of the ratio
unmeasured.why: Two of its three components are published and the third is declared not maintained, so the composite fails on one missing input rather than on incoherence. It also could not honestly be formed by addition even if the third existed, because the two published halves rest on opposite attribution principles: direct tax is assigned to the state code in the assessee's communication address, and goods and services tax is assigned by destination and settled away from the state of collection. The same blanket statement that supplies the stated reason is contradicted by the monthly publication of state-wise goods and services tax, which is why this entry carries the dispute flag.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A single official table adding direct tax, goods and services tax and other indirect tax by state on one declared attribution basis, with the basis stated on its face.

unmeasured.what: State-wise collection of customs duty, union excise duty and service tax
unmeasured.why: The Government states in terms and repeatedly that it does not maintain this. Unlike the blanket claim about indirect taxes as a class, this narrower claim is not contradicted by anything retrieved: no arm of the Government publishes these three heads by state, and the one occasion on which states were ranked by an indirect-tax collection was qualitative and unquantified. The nearest thing to an assertion of impossibility anywhere in either House attaches to the other side of the ratio — expenditure, of which the Government said it is "not maintained and in many case is not possible". On the tax side the word is always not maintained.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs state-wise collection statement on a declared basis, equivalent to the Central Board of Direct Taxes Time Series Data section 1.2.
